hints: Use the $n$th term formula for an AP, $u_n = a + (n - 1)d$, to set up an equation for the 13th term: $a + 12d = 12$.
Use the sum formula $S_n = \frac{n}{2}[2a + (n - 1)d]$ to set up an equation for $S_{30} = -15$.
Solve the simultaneous linear equations to find the first term $a$ and common difference $d$.
Calculate $S_{50}$ using the sum formula with your values of $a$ and $d$.
walkthrough:
Set up the equation for the 13th term using $u_n = a + (n - 1)d$:
$$u_{13} = a + 12d = 12 \quad \text{--- (Equation 1)}$$

Set up the equation for the sum of the first $30$ terms using $S_n = \frac{n}{2}[2a + (n - 1)d]$:
$$S_{30} = \frac{30}{2}[2a + 29d] = 15(2a + 29d) = -15 \implies 2a + 29d = -1 \quad \text{--- (Equation 2)}$$

Solve the simultaneous equations by multiplying Equation 1 by $2$ and subtracting:
$$2(a + 12d) = 2(12) \implies 2a + 24d = 24$$
$$(2a + 29d) - (2a + 24d) = -1 - 24 \implies 5d = -25 \implies d = -5$$
Substitute $d = -5$ back into Equation 1:
$$a + 12(-5) = 12 \implies a - 60 = 12 \implies a = 72$$
